description: Figure 5(a) displays the training loss curves for different methods as a function of training steps, plotted on a linear scale from 0 to 143,000 steps on the x-axis and loss values from approximately 94 to 100 on the y-axis. The plot includes five distinct lines, each representing a different model configuration: Vanilla (purple, solid line with circle markers), StrmLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line with square markers), SepLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line with diamond markers), SepLLM (n=128) (green, solid line with triangle markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H) (red, solid line with inverted triangle markers). All curves begin at a loss value near 100 at step 0 and exhibit a general downward trend as training progresses. The Vanilla model shows the steepest initial decline, reaching a loss of approximately 95.5 by step 143,000. The StrmLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64) curves follow similar trajectories, ending near 96.0 and 96.5, respectively. The SepLLM (n=128) curve declines more gradually, stabilizing around 97.0, while the SepLLM (n=64, H) curve remains the highest, ending near 97.5. The lines are closely spaced, indicating relatively similar convergence behaviors across methods, with the Vanilla model achieving the lowest final loss.
